From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CSM intake: API fallback patterns, retry & throttle guidance

Jordan / team,

Quick pass with practical recommendations you can use immediately. I attached a small .md with snippets (sdk-sample-snippets.md) but pasted the essentials below.

1) Timeouts (recommended):
- TCP connect: 2s
- Request total timeout: 30s for sync generation; 90s for streaming use-cases (stream keep-alive)
- Per-token soft timeout (if available in SDK): ~2s to avoid long blocking tokens

2) Retry policy (idempotent or best-effort generation calls):
- Retry on: 429, 503, 504, network errors (timeout, connection reset), 408
- Dont retry on: 400, 401, 403, 422 (client errors)
- Backoff: exponential with full jitter
  - base_delay = 200ms
  - multiplier = 2.0
  - max_delay = 10s
  - max_attempts = 4 (so up to ~4 retries; tune down for latency-sensitive endpoints)

3) Rate-limit headers we emit (recommended client behavior):
- X-RateLimit-Limit: per-minute token or request limit
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: remaining quota in window
- X-RateLimit-Reset: epoch seconds when quota resets
- 429 responses will include Retry-After (seconds) when applicable

4) Circuit breaker and burst handling:
- Use a token-bucket locally to smooth client bursts before hitting the network
- If Remaining is low, reduce concurrency and backoff aggressively; if Retry-After present, honor it

5) Session continuity / KV cache notes:
- For chat continuity across model variants, persist conversation KV to a durable store (Redis) with session id. Redwood's KV cache is local to serving nodes and not automatically cross-tenant replicated; best practice is to keep a session checkpoint in your store and hydrate on new model instances.
- If you must do a fast cutover, include a short grace period where both endpoints read from the same session store.

6) Dedicated capacity guidance:
- For steady 120 TPS with 500 TPS peaks, Dedicated/reserved nodes are recommended if you need predictable p95 latency SLAs. For variable load with cost-sensitivity, use Hosted with a routing policy + autoscale but set a fallback model variant for latency spikes.

7) Small Java + Go examples (abbreviated):
- Java (OkHttp):
  OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
    .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
    .build();
  // Exponential backoff with jitter wrapper around call

- Go (net/http):
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
  // Retry loop: for attempt := 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++ { ... }

Notes: I included a sample circuit-breaker implementation and a packaged backoff util in sdk-sample-snippets.md.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Implementation plan & cutover options for SummitApps

Hi all,

Attached is a concise implementation runbook and recommended cutover plan. Key pieces below so you can act quickly:

1) Pre-cutover checklist (attach): IP allowlist, staging keys, perf baseline, e2e smoke scripts.
2) Canary options (recommended order):
  a) Internal beta users (5%) -> validate session continuity and latency
  b) Region-based (west-1 only, 25%) -> validate capacity in region
  c) Percent ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48-72 hours) with health gates
3) Health & rollback gates:
  - p95 latency increase > 30% for 15m -> pause rollouts and drop to previous model variant
  - Error rate > 1% 5xx for 10m -> automatic rollback to earlier endpoint
  - Monitoring: Redwood Console link (shared), custom Prometheus job to monitor 429/Retry-After spikes
4) Session continuity:
  - Persist session KV to Redis with TTL (recommended 24h). During cutover both old and new endpoints should read from Redis; write-through for new sessions.
5) Rollback procedure:
  - DNS swap if used: keep low TTL and validate; fallback path: route traffic to legacy path for 30m then cut if stable
  - Path/versioning: prefer versioned routes if you expect long-lived sessions, otherwise DNS swap is simpler but needs TTL planning
6) Estimate for Dedicated capacity provisioning: ~2-3 weeks for committed pools (depending on region). If you need <48h predictability, we recommend a short-term burst capacity plan + canary to mitigate risk.

Next steps: Jordan  I scheduled the 45m handoff for Wed 2027-04-14 14:00 PST and shared a calendar invite. Please confirm. I also uploaded the runbook and the distilled implementation checklist to the Drive link in metadata.

Thanks,
